sources.title: Wuhou Shrine (2026): Three Kingdoms History & Visit Guide
sources.content:
Wuhou Shrine Quick Facts & Logistics:
Location: Wuhou District, Chengdu (south-central, close to city center)
Ticket Price: 50 RMB standard adult admission
Hours: 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM daily (last tickets sold at 5:00 PM)
Requirements: Foreigners must scan physical passports at the gate
Time Needed: Approximately 2 hours for the shrine, plus 1-2 hours for adjacent Jinli Ancient Street
Transportation: Metro Line 3 or 5 to Gaoshengqiao Station (Exit D), then 10-minute walk. Taxi/Didi: ~15-20 RMB from central locations.

Historical Context: Three Kingdoms Period
The shrine commemorates figures from the Three Kingdoms era (220-280 AD) when the Han Dynasty fractured into three competing states: Wei, Wu, and Shu. Chengdu served as capital of the Shu Han kingdom.

Zhuge Liang (Wuhou): A chancellor and military strategist so brilliant that his name is synonymous with genius in modern Chinese. Legendary achievements include weather prediction and inventing an early wheelbarrow. He represents ultimate loyalty in Chinese culture.

Liu Bei: Started as a humble straw sandal weaver, became emperor. Legend states he visited Zhuge Liang's thatched cottage three times in freezing snow to recruit him.

Unique Feature: The only shrine in China where an emperor and his minister are worshiped together in the same space—historically unprecedented in China's strict hierarchy.

Walking Route:
Step 1 - Triple-Success Stele: A massive stone tablet erected in 809 AD during the Tang Dynasty. Named for three perfections: essay, calligraphy, and stone carving.
Step 2 - Hall of Liu Bei: Features his gilded statue plus 28 clay statues of officials lining side corridors.
Step 3 - Hall of Zhuge Liang: Shows him holding his iconic feather fan and wearing a Taoist robe, with statues of his son and grandson.
Step 4 - Liu Bei's Tomb (Huiling): A massive, circular grassy mound surrounded by a brick wall containing Liu Bei and two empresses, never excavated.

The Famous Red Wall Photography Spot:
Description: A long, winding pedestrian pathway with striking, saturated vermilion red walls beneath towering bamboo forests creating intoxicating color contrast.
Timing Strategy: Arrive at 9:00 AM opening to photograph before crowds arrive.
Best Light Conditions: Overcast days produce superior results; diffused lighting makes the red pop brilliantly.
Composition Tip: Use the gentle S-curve of the wall as a leading line with subjects wearing neutral clothing.

Jinli Ancient Street Connection: The shrine shares an eastern wall with Jinli Ancient Street. Simply follow the signs to the Jinli Exit to transition directly into the adjacent marketplace.

Street Food Recommendations: Three Great Cannons (sticky rice dessert coated in roasted soybean powder), Bobo Chicken (wooden skewers in cold numbing-and-spicy red chili oil), Spicy Rabbit Head (rabbit skull stewed in intense spices).

sources.title: Wuhou Shrine Travel Guide - Sichuan Travel Guide
sources.content:
Wuhou Shrine, also known as Han Zhaolie Temple or Memorial of Zhugeliang, honors a famous Chinese Prime Minister from the Three Kingdoms period (approximately 18 centuries ago). It was built in 223 AD when people started to build a tomb for Liu Bei, the king of Shu. This temple holds unique significance as the only one temple in China that has a king and a minister in a temple together.

Main Attractions:
Han Zhaolie Temple: Houses a 3-meter statue of Liu Bei, the Shu Kingdom's ruler.
Zhuge Liang Temple (Wuhou Shrine): The primary temple featuring Zhuge Liang, described as not only a wise prime minister, he was also an inventor, a successful military talent, a smart politician, and a respected leader.
Wen and Wu Pavilion: Walking area displaying statues of 28 important Shu Kingdom figures, including military generals like Zhaoyun and Machao.
Liu Bei's Tomb (Hui Ling): An economical burial site, personally selected by Zhuge Liang.
Sanyi Temple: Dedicated to three sworn brothers—Liu, Guan, and Zhang—with Guan symbolizing loyalty in Chinese culture.
Nanjiao Park: Originally separate, now integrated with the shrine; features tea houses and occasional art galleries.

Visiting Information:
Location: Central Chengdu, adjacent to Jinli Old Street
Hours: Summer 8:00-21:30; Winter 8:00-18:30
Access: Bus routes 1, 10, 57, 82, 301, 334, 335, 123, 521, 901, 904; taxi available

sources.title: Exploring Wuhou Shrine: A Journey Through Chengdu's Historic Red Walls
sources.content:
The Wu Hou Shrine stands as one of Chengdu's most revered historical treasures, honoring the legendary strategist Zhuge Liang and his lord Liu Bei, offering visitors a profound journey through China's Three Kingdoms period (220-280 CE).

Visit Experience & Duration: Most visitors spend 2-3 hours exploring the complex thoroughly, though history enthusiasts might want to allocate a full half-day. The classic route involves walking through the main entrance, visiting the Main Hall, seeing Liu Bei's Tomb, passing by famous statues and old relics, finishing in about 1.5 hours.

Main Attractions: Inside stands a 3-meter-tall golden statue of Liu Bei seated with dignity, with his grandson Liu Chen to his left, and statues of Liu Bei's loyal generals Guan Yu and Zhang Fei placed on the east and west sides respectively. Zhuge Liang is the highlight of the Wuhou experience, with his golden sculpture positioned in the center of the building with his son and grandson at the back.

Atmosphere & Surroundings: The environment surrounding the Wuhou Shrine is both tranquil and steeped in history, with the temple embraced by lush greenery, particularly ancient cypress and pine trees, and the air carrying the earthy scent of the woods.

Timing: If you want a clean photo without 50 strangers in the background, you must arrive exactly when the gates open at 9:00 AM.

sources.title: 武侯祠 - 百度百科
sources.content:
武侯祠位于四川省成都市武侯区武侯祠大街231号，占地面积15万平方米（230亩），是纪念刘备、诸葛亮等蜀汉英雄人物的祠庙。1961年3月4日被中华人民共和国国务院公布为第一批全国重点文物保护单位。

历史沿革：
蜀汉时期：蜀汉章武元年（221年），惠陵、汉昭烈庙始建。
南北朝：武侯祠始建，与惠陵、汉昭烈庙位于同一区域。
明代：洪武二十四年（1391年），蜀献王朱椿主张君臣宜一体，废弃惠陵旁的武侯祠，将诸葛亮像移入汉昭烈庙内，实现一祠同祀君臣的格局。
清代：康熙十至十一年（1671-1672年），四川按察使宋可法主持重建武侯祠，形成前后两殿并立的格局。
现代：1949年后由政府接管；1984年成立成都武侯祠博物馆；2003年将武侯祠与南郊公园合并；2008年汶川地震造成古建筑部分受损；2022年6月28日发现8通清代碑刻。

建筑格局：武侯祠由四部分组成：汉昭烈庙、武侯祠、惠陵、三义庙。属于成都武侯祠博物馆的文化遗产保护区。

sources.title: Wu Hou Shrine: Complete 2026 Guide + Insider Tips
sources.content:
Wuhou Temple is dedicated to Zhuge Liang, the Marquis Wu (Wuhou) of the Kingdom of Shu in the Three Kingdoms Period (220-280). It holds the unique distinction of being the only temple that jointly honors a ruler and his minister: Liu Bei, the emperor of Shu Han, and his prime minister Zhuge Liang.

Getting There: Take Metro Line 3 and get off at Gaoshengqiao, then walk eastwards along Wuhouci Avenue for 3-5 minutes. Alternatively, take buses 1, 57, 77, 82, 334, 335 to Wuhouci Station.

Hours & Admission: Opening Hours 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM (Ticket sales stop at 5:00 PM). Standard entrance fee is 50 RMB. You must bring your physical passport to purchase tickets.

The site is big and takes several hours to explore for a deep understanding, though those who want to see only the main highlights can cover the visit in just an hour.

The shrine's location makes it easy to combine with visits to the Wide and Narrow Alleys or the Jinli Ancient Street, both within walking distance.
